questions.q: C-Cl bond in methyl chloride compared to C-Cl bond in chlorobenzene is
questions.explanation: In chlorobenzene, resonance gives the C-Cl bond partial double-bond character, making it shorter and stronger than the pure single C-Cl bond in methyl chloride; so methyl chloride's bond is comparatively longer and weaker.

questions.q: The compound from which chlorobenzene cannot be prepared easily is
questions.explanation: Phenol's C-OH bond has partial double-bond character and resists nucleophilic substitution, so it cannot easily be converted to chlorobenzene, unlike benzene (direct chlorination), aniline or benzenediazonium chloride (via Sandmeyer reaction).

questions.q: In S$_N$1 reaction, the alkyl halide that on hydrolysis produces racemic mixture is
questions.explanation: 2-Bromobutane has a chiral centre; S$_N$1 hydrolysis proceeds via a planar carbocation attacked equally from both faces, giving a racemic mixture. The other alkyl halides listed are achiral at the reacting carbon.

questions.q: The organic compound [a benzene ring with a -C(CH$_3$)$_2$Cl group attached to it] can be classified as ________
questions.explanation: The halogen-bearing carbon is attached directly to the benzene ring but is itself sp$^3$ (not part of the ring), which is the defining feature of a benzylic halide.

questions.q: Chlorobenzene reacts with bromine gas in the presence of Anhyd. AlBr$_3$ to yield p-Bromochlorobenzene. This reaction is classified as ____
questions.explanation: AlBr$_3$ generates an electrophilic Br$^+$ species that substitutes a ring hydrogen on chlorobenzene, a classic electrophilic aromatic substitution.

questions.q: The organometallic compound (CH$_3$)$_3$CMgBr on reaction with D$_2$O produces ____
questions.explanation: Grignard reagents react with D$_2$O by deuterolysis of the C-Mg bond, replacing -MgBr with -D to give (CH$_3$)$_3$CD.

questions.q: The major product formed when 1-Bromo-3-chlorocyclobutane reacts with metallic sodium in dry ether is [structures shown: (1) bromocyclobutane; (2) chlorocyclobutane; (3) plain cyclobutane; (4) a bicyclic structure -- a cyclobutane ring with an extra diagonal bond across it, i.e. bicyclo[1.1.0]butane]
questions.explanation: Intramolecular Wurtz-type coupling (Freund reaction) of the two halogens on the same ring with sodium forms a new C-C bond across the ring, giving the fused bicyclic product bicyclo[1.1.0]butane.

questions.q: In the following scheme of reactions: C$_2$H$_5$Cl $\xrightarrow{X}$ C$_2$H$_5$F; C$_2$H$_5$Cl $\xrightarrow{Y}$ CH$_2$=CH$_2$; C$_2$H$_5$Cl $\xrightarrow{Z}$ C$_4$H$_{10}$. X, Y and Z respectively are:
options: HF, aqueous KOH and Na in dry ether
Hg$_2$F$_2$, alcoholic KOH and Na in dry ether
questions.explanation: Hg$_2$F$_2$ converts C$_2$H$_5$Cl to C$_2$H$_5$F (Swarts reaction); alcoholic KOH causes dehydrohalogenation to ethene; Na in dry ether gives the Wurtz coupling product butane.

questions.q: A haloalkane undergoes S$_N$2 or S$_N$1 reaction depending on
questions.explanation: The polarity and ionising power of the solvent determine whether substitution proceeds via the S$_N$1 or S$_N$2 pathway.

questions.q: 2-Methyl propane can be prepared by Wurtz reaction. The haloalkanes taken along with metallic sodium and dry ether are:
questions.explanation: Wurtz coupling of chloromethane and 2-chloropropane with Na/dry ether gives 2-methylpropane.

questions.q: Identify A, B and C in the sequence: CH$_3$CH$_2$Br $\xrightarrow[alc]{KCN}$ A $\xrightarrow{LiAlH_4}$ B $\xrightarrow[0^\circ C]{HNO_2}$ C
questions.explanation: Alcoholic KCN gives the alkyl cyanide CH$_3$CH$_2$CN (A); LiAlH$_4$ reduces the nitrile to the primary amine CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$NH$_2$ (B); HNO$_2$ at 0$^\circ$C converts the amine to the alcohol CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$OH (C) via an unstable diazonium salt.

questions.q: Which of the following is an organometallic compound?
questions.explanation: An organometallic compound has a direct carbon-metal bond; ethylmagnesium bromide (a Grignard reagent) has a C-Mg bond, while the others are ionic salts with O-metal bonds.

questions.q: Propene is treated with (i) HBr in the presence of benzoyl peroxide to give A (major product), and (ii) HI to give B (major product). Identify A and B in the reaction
questions.explanation: HBr in the presence of peroxide adds anti-Markovnikov (peroxide/Kharasch effect) to give 1-bromopropane (A); HI shows no peroxide effect, so it adds Markovnikov to give 2-iodopropane (B).

questions.q: In the following pairs of halogen compounds, which compound undergoes faster S$_N^1$ reaction? Pair (i): (CH$_3$)$_3$C-Cl [2-chloro-2-methylpropane] and CH$_3$-CH$_2$-CHCl-CH$_2$-CH$_3$ [a secondary chloropentane]. Pair (ii): CH$_3$-CH$_2$-CHCl-CH$_2$-CH$_3$ type chain with Cl on an internal, more-substituted carbon, and CH$_3$-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-Cl [a straight-chain primary chloride with Cl at the end]
options: (i) the secondary chloride ; (ii) the primary (terminal-Cl) chloride
(i) the secondary chloride ; (ii) the branched (more-substituted) chloride
(i) the tertiary chloride ; (ii) the primary (terminal-Cl) chloride
(i) the tertiary chloride ; (ii) the branched (more-substituted) chloride
questions.explanation: S$_N^1$ reactions proceed through a carbocation intermediate, so in each pair the more substituted halide (tertiary in pair (i), and the more branched/internal chloride in pair (ii)) reacts faster, since more substituted carbocations are more stable.

questions.q: Which one of the following Chlorohydrocarbon readily undergoes solvolysis?
questions.explanation: Benzyl chloride ionizes readily (S$_N^1$) because the resulting benzylic carbocation is resonance-stabilized by the aromatic ring; vinylic and aryl chlorides resist solvolysis, and the phenethyl chloride's C-Cl carbon is not directly benzylic.

questions.q: Identify the products A and B in the reactions: R-X + AgCN $\rightarrow$ A + AgX ; R-X + KCN $\rightarrow$ B + KX
questions.explanation: AgCN is covalent and its N-end attacks R-X (kinetically preferred), giving the isocyanide RNC as A; KCN is ionic and its more nucleophilic C-end attacks, giving the nitrile RCN as B.

questions.q: The order of reactivity of the compounds C$_6$H$_5$CH$_2$Br, C$_6$H$_5$CH(C$_6$H$_5$)Br, C$_6$H$_5$CH(CH$_3$)Br and C$_6$H$_5$C(CH$_3$)(C$_6$H$_5$)Br in S$_N$2 reaction is
questions.explanation: S$_N$2 rate decreases as steric bulk around the reacting carbon increases, so the least hindered primary benzylic bromide (C$_6$H$_5$CH$_2$Br) reacts fastest and the most substituted one reacts slowest.

questions.q: Prolonged exposure of chloroform in humans may cause damage to liver. It is due to the formation of the following compound:
questions.explanation: Chloroform is slowly oxidised by air/light to the highly toxic gas phosgene (COCl$_2$), which damages the liver.

questions.q: Which of the following halide shows highest reactivity towards S$_N$1 reaction?
questions.explanation: Benzyl chloride ionises readily because the resulting benzylic carbocation is stabilised by resonance with the ring, giving the fastest S$_N$1 reaction; aryl halides resist S$_N$1 altogether.

questions.q: In the reaction: [a branched secondary alkyl magnesium bromide]-MgBr + CH$_3$NH$_2$ $\xrightarrow{\text{Dry ether}}$ X. The number of possible isomers for the organic compound X is
questions.explanation: The acidic N-H of methylamine protonates the Grignard reagent at its chiral carbon; since the carbanion-like carbon can be attacked from either face, the resulting alkane X is obtained as a mixture of 2 stereoisomers (as per KEA key).

questions.q: Which of the following halide undergoes hydrolysis on warming with water/aqueous NaOH?
options: 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene (picryl chloride, Cl with NO$_2$ at 2,4,6 positions)
questions.explanation: Electron-withdrawing -NO2 groups ortho/para to the C-Cl bond activate the ring for nucleophilic aromatic substitution; with three -NO2 groups (2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene) hydrolysis occurs most readily, even on warming with water.

questions.q: The compound having longest C-Cl bond is
questions.explanation: In chlorobenzene, p-nitrochlorobenzene and vinyl chloride, the C-Cl bond has partial double-bond character from conjugation with the pi system, shortening it; in 3-chlorocyclohexene the Cl is on an sp3 carbon with no such conjugation, so its C-Cl bond is the longest.

questions.q: The alkyl halides required to prepare 2-methylpentane, (CH$_3$)$_2$CHCH$_2$CH$_2$CH$_3$, by Wurtz reaction are
questions.explanation: Cross Wurtz coupling of isopropyl chloride, (CH3)2CHCl, with n-propyl chloride, CH3CH2CH2Cl, joins the two fragments to give (CH3)2CH-CH2CH2CH3, i.e. 2-methylpentane.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true in case of alkyl halides ?
options: They are highly soluble in water
questions.explanation: The C-X bond in alkyl halides is polar due to the electronegativity difference; they cannot hydrogen bond with water, are poorly soluble in water, and being saturated do not undergo addition reactions.

questions.q: n-Propyl chloride reacts with sodium metal in dry ether to give
questions.explanation: This is a Wurtz reaction: 2CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$Cl + 2Na $\to$ CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$-CH$_2$CH$_2$CH$_3$ (n-hexane) + 2NaCl.

questions.q: Tertiary alkyl halide is practically inert to substitution by S$_N$2 mechanism because of
questions.explanation: The three bulky alkyl groups around the carbon bearing the halogen block backside attack by the nucleophile, so tertiary halides resist S$_N$2 substitution due to steric hindrance.

questions.q:
In the following sequence of reactions

CH$_3$Br $\xrightarrow{KCN}$ A $\xrightarrow{H_3O^+}$ B $\xrightarrow{LiAlH_4}$ C

The end product C is
questions.explanation: CH$_3$Br + KCN → CH$_3$CN (A); H$_3$O$^+$ hydrolysis of the nitrile gives CH$_3$COOH (B); LiAlH$_4$ reduction of the acid gives CH$_3$CH$_2$OH (C), i.e. ethyl alcohol.

questions.q: IUPAC name of the compound H$_3$C-CH=CH-CH$_2$Br [but-2-ene with a bromomethyl group replacing one terminal H] is,
questions.explanation: The structure CH$_3$-CH=CH-CH$_2$Br is numbered to give the double bond the lowest locant: 1-bromobut-2-ene.

questions.q: Replacement of Cl of Chlorobenzene to give phenol requires drastic conditions, but Cl of 2, 4 - dinitro chlorobenzene is readily replaced. This is because,
options: $-$NO$_2$ group makes the ring electron rich at ortho and para positions.
$-$NO$_2$ group withdraws electrons from meta position.
$-$NO$_2$ withdraws electrons from ortho and para positions.
questions.explanation: The $-$NO$_2$ groups withdraw electron density from the ortho/para carbon bearing Cl, stabilising the intermediate and favouring nucleophilic aromatic substitution.

questions.q: Reactivity of order of halides for dehydrohalogenation is
options: R – F > R – Cl > R – Br > R – I
R – I > R – Br > R – Cl > R – F
R – I > R – Cl > R – Br > R – F
R – F > R – I > R – Br > R – Cl
questions.explanation: The weaker C$-$I bond breaks most easily, so reactivity for elimination follows R$-$I > R$-$Br > R$-$Cl > R$-$F.

questions.q: The hydrolysis of optically active 2-bromobutane with aqueous NaOH result in the formation of
questions.explanation: A secondary halide like 2-bromobutane reacts by a mixture of SN1 and SN2 pathways, so the chiral centre is partially inverted and partially retained, giving a racemic mixture, ($\pm$) butan-2-ol.

questions.q: $\bigcirc$-Br + Mg $\xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}}$ A $\xrightarrow[\text{H}^+]{\text{H}_2\text{O}}$ B. (cyclohexyl bromide reacting with Mg then aqueous acid) The product 'B' is
questions.explanation: Cyclohexyl bromide with Mg in dry ether forms the Grignard reagent A (cyclohexylmagnesium bromide); simple aqueous acid workup (protonolysis, not addition to a carbonyl) converts the highly basic C-Mg bond directly into a C-H bond, giving cyclohexane (B).

questions.q: The arrangement of following compounds: i. bromomethane ii. bromoform iii. chloromethane iv. dibromomethane, in the increasing order of their boiling point is
questions.explanation: Boiling point rises with molecular mass/number and size of halogen atoms: chloromethane (-24$^\circ$C) < bromomethane (3.6$^\circ$C) < dibromomethane (97$^\circ$C) < bromoform (149$^\circ$C), i.e. iii < i < iv < ii.

questions.q:
The compound that reacts the fastest with sodium methoxide is

[four chlorobenzene derivatives with a leaving group Cl and NO$_2$ substituent(s): (1) Cl and NO$_2$ para to each other; (2) Cl only, no NO$_2$; (3) Cl with NO$_2$ para and another position; (4) Cl with NO$_2$ ortho and NO$_2$ para (two NO$_2$ groups activating the ring for nucleophilic substitution)]
options: chloro-dinitrobenzene (NO$_2$ groups not both activating the Cl position)
1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (Cl with NO$_2$ groups ortho and para to it)
questions.explanation: Nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) on aryl halides is accelerated by electron-withdrawing NO$_2$ groups ortho/para to the leaving group; the compound with two NO$_2$ groups ortho and para to Cl reacts fastest with sodium methoxide.

questions.q: An incorrect statement with respect to S$_N$1 and S$_N$2 mechanisms for alkyl halide is
options: A weak nucleophile and a protic solvent increases the rate or favours S$_N$1 reaction.
S$_N$1 reactions can be catalysed by some Lewis acids.
Competing reaction for an S$_N$2 reaction is rearrangement.
A strong nucleophile in an aprotic solvent increases the rate or favours S$_N$2 reaction.
questions.explanation: Rearrangement (via carbocation) is a competing pathway for S$_N$1, not S$_N$2, which proceeds through a concerted backside attack with no carbocation intermediate; so statement (3) is incorrect.

questions.q: An alkyl bromide (X) reacts with Sodium in ether to form 4, 5-diethyl octane, the compound 'X' is
questions.explanation: Wurtz coupling of two molecules of 3-bromohexane (CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$CHBrCH$_2$CH$_3$) joins at the C-Br carbons, giving an 8-carbon chain with ethyl branches at C4 and C5, i.e., 4,5-diethyloctane.

questions.q:
Which of the following pairs are correctly matched ?
I. RX + AgOH$_{(aq)}$ $ightarrow$ RH
II. RX + AgCN$_{(alco)}$ $ightarrow$ RNC
III. RX + KCN$_{(alco)}$ $ightarrow$ RNC
IV. RX + Na$_{(ether)}$ $ightarrow$ R-R
questions.explanation: AgCN (covalent, Ag-C bond) gives isocyanide (RNC) as major product, and RX with Na in ether undergoes the Wurtz reaction (R-R); so II and IV are correctly matched.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT formed when a mixture of methyl bromide and bromobenzene is heated with sodium metal in the presence of dry Ether?
questions.explanation: Wurtz-Fittig reaction of CH$_3$Br and C$_6$H$_5$Br with Na gives ethane (CH$_3$-CH$_3$), toluene (CH$_3$-C$_6$H$_5$) and diphenyl (C$_6$H$_5$-C$_6$H$_5$); propane cannot form from these two reactants.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT TRUE for S$_N$1 reaction?
options: 3° − alkyl halides generally react through S$_N$1 reaction.
The rate of the reaction does not depend upon the molar concentration of the nucleophile.
1° − alkyl halides generally react through S$_N$1 reaction.
questions.explanation: S$_N$1 reactions proceed via a stable carbocation, favoured by 3° alkyl halides; 1° alkyl halides do not readily undergo S$_N$1, so statement (4) is false.

questions.q: The maximum number of possible optical isomers in 1-bromo-2-methyl cyclobutane is ...
questions.explanation: The molecule has two stereocentres (C1 bearing Br and C2 bearing methyl) with no symmetry in the ring, giving $2^2=4$ stereoisomers (two pairs of enantiomers, cis and trans).

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT TRUE for the hydrolysis of $t$-butyl bromide with aqueous $NaOH$?
options: The intermediate formed is a carbocation.
Rate of the reaction doubles when the concentration of alkali is doubled.
Rate of the reaction doubles when the concentration of $t$-butyl bromide is doubled.
questions.explanation: The reaction proceeds by $S_N1$, so its rate depends only on the substrate concentration, not on $[OH^-]$; hence doubling the alkali concentration does not double the rate.

questions.q:
Following is the substitution reaction in which $-CN$ replaces $-Cl$.
$R-Cl+KCN\xrightarrow[\text{(alcoholic)}]{\Delta}R-CN+KCl$
To obtain propanenitrile, $R-Cl$ should be ..................
questions.explanation: Propanenitrile is $CH_3CH_2CN$ (3 carbons including the nitrile carbon), so $R=C_2H_5$, meaning $R-Cl$ is chloroethane.

questions.q: Reaction of methyl bromide with aqueous sodium hydroxide involves ...................
questions.explanation: Methyl bromide is a primary halide with no steric hindrance and reacts with a strong nucleophile (OH$^-$) via the bimolecular $S_N2$ mechanism.

questions.q: Which one of the following forms propanenitrile as the major product?
questions.explanation: Alcoholic KCN reacts via the nucleophilic cyanide carbon (C-attack) with ethyl bromide to give ethyl cyanide (propanenitrile, CH$_3$CH$_2$CN); AgCN, being covalent, favours N-attack to give isocyanides instead.

questions.q: IUPAC name of (CH$_3$)$_3$CCl
questions.explanation: (CH$_3$)$_3$CCl is named systematically as 2-chloro-2-methylpropane.

questions.q: The compound which forms acetaldehyde when heated with dilute NaOH is
questions.explanation: The gem-dihalide CH$_3$CHCl$_2$ (1,1-dichloroethane) hydrolyses with dilute NaOH to give acetaldehyde.
